title: Personalized Antiplatelet Therapy to Prevent Recurrent Cardiovascular Events After Ischemic Stroke
official: Tailored Antiplatelet Secondary Prevention in Non-cardioembolic Ischemic Stroke: a Phase IV Gender-stratified Randomized Controlled Trial (TAILOR Trial)
summary:
The TAILOR study aims to determine whether personalized antiplatelet therapy can reduce the risk of recurrent major cardiovascular events in patients who have experienced (a non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke).

Antiplatelet medications, such as aspirin and clopidogrel, are commonly prescribed to prevent stroke recurrence. However, some patients do not respond adequately to these medications and may remain at increased risk of further cardiovascular events.

The study will compare two approaches to antiplatelet therapy: standard care, in which medications are prescribed according to current clinical practice, and personalized care (tailored care), in which treatment is adjusted based on a blood test measuring how effectively the medication inhibits platelet activity.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of these two treatment strategies and followed for 12 months.

The main hypothesis is that tailoring antiplatelet therapy according to individual platelet response will be more effective than standard care in preventing recurrent ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular death. The study will also explore potential differences in treatment response between women and men.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Aged ≥18 years
* Males and females
* Non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke within the previous 14 days
* Starting or continuing secondary prevention with single or dual antiplatelet therapy after the index stroke
* Written informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Known hypersensitivity to aspirin, clopidogrel or ticlopidine, or to any of the excipients.
* Concurrent need for anticoagulation for any indication.
* Contraindication to study drugs.
* Indications to perform carotid revascularization surgery.
* Participation in a clinical trial in which an investigational drug was administered within 30 days of screening or within the 5 half-lives of the study drug, whichever is longer.
* Pregnancy and breastfeeding; WOCBP (Women of Childbearing Potential) not using acceptable contraception during the trial period (combined \[estrogen- and progestogen-containing\] hormonal contraception associated with inhibition of ovulation, progestogen-only hormonal contraception associated with inhibition of ovulation, intrauterine device \[IUD\], intrauterine hormone-releasing system \[IUS\], bilateral tubal occlusion, vasectomised partner, sexual abstinence, progestogen-only oral hormonal contraception where inhibition of ovulation is not the primary mode of action, male or female condom with or without spermicide, cap, diaphragm, or sponge with spermicide).
* History of asthma induced by the administration of acetylsalicylates or substances with a similar activity, especially nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.
* Active or previous recurrent peptic ulcer and/or gastric/intestinal bleeding, or other types of bleeding such as cerebrovascular hemorrhage.
* Bleeding diathesis; coagulation disorders such as hemophilia and thrombocytopenia.
* Severe hepatic impairment.
* Severe renal impairment.
* Uncontrolled severe cardiac failure.
* Methotrexate used at doses equal to or greater than 15 mg/week. Combination with other potentially myelotoxic drugs. Subjects with or who have had leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, or agranulocytosis.
